evidence: [Issue 22627](https://github.com/rocq-prover/rocq/issues/22627) contains the concise proposal and a minimal example distinguishing two roots with different assumptions.

[The earlier repeated-query report, issue 5639](https://github.com/rocq-prover/rocq/issues/5639), [the maintainer recommendation on closed PR 22610](https://github.com/rocq-prover/rocq/pull/22610#issuecomment-6342792902) and [PR 22425’s shared-proof-term traversal work](https://github.com/rocq-prover/rocq/pull/22425) supply the closely related upstream context.

Acceptance distinguishes roots through types, sealed implementations, sections, repeated roots and unsafe flags, preserving exact per-root assumptions and context identity. Performance claims require separate measurements.

items.topic: Trap illegal vector-memory EMUL combinations before dependent assertions
items.benefit: Prevents the curated integer-vector oracle from aborting on an illegal memory instruction that should report an architectural illegal-instruction result.
items.review: The retained VLSEGTYPE, VSSEGTYPE, VLSSEGTYPE and VSSSEGTYPE clauses assert that EMUL_pow lies in [-3, 3] before their Illegal_Instruction checks. With e8,m8 and EEW64, the expression computes 6; nf=1 includes ordinary unit-stride instructions. This is a static source finding, not an executed local reproduction. Issue 1800 already covers it. Attempted PR 1828 is closed without merge and bundled the exception repair with optional NaN behavior; no matching open repair was found. The broader issue catalogue and specification-permitted NaN differences are outside this item.
items.next_action: Reproduce the retained integer-memory cases, then coordinate a narrow legality-before-assertion repair under issue 1800 with valid controls and preserved capability fault ordering.
evidence: [The curated memory clauses](../../model/model/extensions/V/vext_mem_insts.sail) retain the assertion ordering; the relevant path does not require floating-point extensions.

[The upstream diagnosis in issue 1800](https://github.com/riscv/sail-riscv/issues/1800) identifies the memory assertions. [PR 1828](https://github.com/riscv/sail-riscv/pull/1828) is closed unmerged; the current upstream source still contains the assertion ordering at observation.

Acceptance covers lower and upper invalid EMUL combinations and adjacent valid controls for each retained form, architectural state at the trap and capability permission/fault precedence. A new upstream pin alone supplies no local model qualification.

items.topic: Add generator-backed Zicond instruction models
items.benefit: Supplies the missing czero.eqz and czero.nez reference models explicitly owed by R2, without enlarging its scalar instruction scope.
items.review: R2 includes Zicond and currently requires wrapper models written from the curated execute clause because upstream has none. The recursive tree at upstream main c992aa61fdfe0846c5ed90324c596202a1c69b76 contains no Zicond/czero models; all-state issue/PR searches for zicond and czero each returned no match on 2026-10-22. This is an unfiled support proposal, separate from the signed division, xperm and REMUW repairs.
items.next_action: Propose generator and regenerated RV32/RV64 models plus instruction-list support, and qualify them against the curated Sail clause before retiring any R2 wrapper obligation.
evidence: [The R2 smoke contract](../assurance/rtl-cosimulation-harness.md#7-the-bounded-model-checking-smoke) and [MODELS_OWED](../../tools/vos/bmc.py) explicitly name the missing conditional-zero forms.
[The curated Zicond execute clause](../../model/model/extensions/Zicond/zicond_insts.sail) supplies an independent comparison target. No upstream implementation or test was run for this proposal.

Acceptance covers both opcodes, zero/nonzero value and condition, RV64 conditions nonzero only in the upper half, rd=x0, operand/destination aliases and encoding refusal controls. Generator and generated outputs must agree. Bounded smoke evidence remains distinct from hardware refinement.

items.topic: Repair inconsistent robust-security premises and the theorem join
items.benefit: Addresses F-520 and U-25’s missing robust-preservation join, whose current RSC assumptions imply False and cannot be reused for the certifying compiler.
items.review: Issue 21 remains open and assigned to jeremyThibault. Missing linkability and other premises make recomposition and link_compatible inconsistent; degenerate source contexts also weaken the intended security claim. No matching repair was found among the open PRs. PR 20 restores builds and repairs return-event blame while preserving these axioms. Tracked PR 27 removes a different unused axiom and does not repair this theorem.
items.next_action: Coordinate a staged repair using the actual component theorems and explicit source-context guarantees; retain nonlinkable and degenerate-context counterexamples before considering proof reuse.
evidence: [The SECOMP proof-reuse assessment](../assurance/proof-reuse/languages.md#secomp-robust-preservation-components-with-an-unfinished-join) and [U-25](../assurance/unassigned-proof-map.md#7-the-next-slices) explicitly refuse the inconsistent RSC assumptions.

[PR 20](https://github.com/secure-compilation/SECOMP/pull/20) is a build/theorem-maintenance change, not a soundness repair for issue 21. The ccs-main branch remains at cbef9c338d23f40db5054c9a3d6f2b3b873e9204 at observation; no independent upstream build was run.

Acceptance requires a checked composition over justified premises and the local arbitrary-context, observation, declassification and progress mapping. A repaired upstream statement alone does not establish CJ-SECOMP.

items.topic: Replace the false admitted back-translation bridge step_fix_fix
items.benefit: Addresses F-520’s independent back-translation inconsistency, so the compiler security proof does not inherit a false admitted simulation premise.
items.review: Issue 26 remains open, assigned to jeremyThibault and dongjaelee1. The admitted lemma converts ordinary assembly runs into runs satisfying additional checks; the report provides machine-checked counterexamples including public pointer memory and cross-compartment calls. No matching repair PR was found. PR 19 leaves the back-translation theorem statements and assumptions unchanged; old PR 1 contains the unfinished proof rather than a repair for this report. This remains independent of candidate 35’s RSC theorem join.
items.next_action: Agree on a semantics/proof repair covering required programs and adversarial contexts, preserve the reported counterexamples, and keep any narrower theorem restrictions explicit during U-25 qualification.
evidence: [F-520’s proof-reuse record](../assurance/proof-reuse/languages.md#secomp-robust-preservation-components-with-an-unfinished-join) and [U-25](../assurance/unassigned-proof-map.md#7-the-next-slices) prohibit reusing results resting on step_fix_fix.

[PR 19](https://github.com/secure-compilation/SECOMP/pull/19) explicitly preserves theorem statements/assumptions; [PR 1](https://github.com/secure-compilation/SECOMP/pull/1) is the original unfinished back-translation work. No independent upstream build was run.

Acceptance retains public-pointer, public-struct-copy, signature and builtin-register counterexamples and checks the informative-trace assumptions. A scalar-only public-memory restriction cannot silently satisfy VerifiedOS’s broader robust-preservation obligation.

items.topic: Correct the Core 3.0 administrative-frame typing rule
items.benefit: Repairs the mandatory Core 3.0 semantic reference Q34g must curate for the first-release guest engine, before treating its administrative-frame typing rule as soundness evidence.
items.review: Open PR replaces a contradictory RETURN premise in Instr_ok2/frame with the result type installed in the inner context. Frame_ok otherwise leaves RETURN empty. Both the Core 3.0 and wasm-latest rules change; the exact semantic edition cited by the local assessment still contains the old rule. A maintainer asks whether Frame_ok itself should populate RETURN instead, so the final formulation remains under discussion. This repairs a published specification rule, not a completed Rocq Core 3.0 soundness theorem or a measured local interpreter failure.
items.next_action: Track the agreed rule formulation; Q34g must qualify the selected Core 3.0 edition and its frame/return preservation cases before consuming generated semantics or proof claims.
evidence: [Q34g’s first-release obligation](implementation-checklist.md) requires complete Core 3.0 semantics and both engine theorems; [the semantic-upstream assessment](../assurance/proof-reuse/parsers.md#other-source-leads) records that the inspected specification tree supplies no tracked Rocq proof files.

The specification edition already cited by that assessment, 95dffb694caa11c3663203f2756dda9bf24c2021, still requires C′.RETURN to equal the frame result type before checking the body in C′. The proposed repair checks the body under the explicitly extended context.

Acceptance checks nested frames, explicit returns and result typing against the pinned semantic edition and complete engine proof. Upstream checks and a rule merge alone do not establish local guest confinement.

items.topic: Make memory64/table64 corpus generators exercise 64-bit indices
items.benefit: Prevents Q34g’s shared official corpus from reporting memory64/table64 coverage when generated tests still instantiate 32-bit memories or tables.
items.review: Open PR corrects the memory.copy, table.copy and table.init generators and their 64-bit output, and adds mixed memory32/memory64 copy validation cases. The official corpus edition already cited by the local contract predates this unmerged correction; its table.init generator still hardcodes i32 forms. This is a concrete coverage gap in required first-release features, not evidence that the local engine currently executes them incorrectly.
items.next_action: Track upstream landing and qualify corrected generators, emitted module widths and mixed-width negative cases in Q34g’s single fixture manifest before counting 64-bit coverage.
evidence: [The shared upstream corpus contract](contracts/wasm-execution.md#shared-upstream-corpus) selects official tests/generators and gives Q34g ownership of one feature-mapped fixture manifest. Full Core 3.0 explicitly includes memory64/table64.

The cited corpus edition, 608711107b7f1edb13efd57b7d79b49477462d36, has a table.init generator without the proposed INDEX_TYPE parameterization. The diff changes declarations, offsets and instruction operands together rather than renaming fixtures.

Acceptance inspects decoded feature usage and positive/invalid mixed-width cases, records generator and module identities, and filters the exact Core 3.0 scope. A newer upstream main test tree is not automatically the selected semantic edition or a local qualification verdict.
